learn.hook: Draw a circle freehand, then with a compass. Which one is truly round?
points: Freehand drawing is quick for sketches, but a ruler and compass give exact lengths and perfect circles.
In maths, a curve is any shape you can draw without lifting your pencil. Straight lines and circles are curves too!
Some curves close up (a circle), some don't (a wavy line). Some are straight (a line segment), some bend.
A ruler makes straight curves (line segments); a compass makes round curves (circles and arcs).

example.q: Is the letter S a curve? Is the letter i (with its dot)?
steps: S can be drawn in one stroke without lifting the pencil: it is a curve.
For i you must lift the pencil to put the dot, so as a whole it is not a single curve.
example.answer: S yes; i is not one curve

learn.reallife: Engineers draw building plans with exact tools, but start with freehand sketches to think.

items: Circle
Line segment
Letter C

An equals sign =

games.title: Curves
items: A straight line segment is a curve in maths.
It is drawn without lifting the pencil.
A circle is a curve.
Drawn in one go.
Freehand circles are always perfectly round.
A compass gives a true circle.
A compass draws circles and arcs.
That is its job.
The letter L is one curve.
Down then across without lifting.

quiz.q: Which is a curve in the mathematical sense?
quiz.explain: A curve is anything drawn without lifting the pencil, including straight lines.
steps: In maths, a curve is anything drawn without lifting the pencil.
A straight line segment is drawn in one stroke, so it is a curve too.
Two dots, '=' and a dotted line need the pencil lifted.
So the straight line segment is a curve.
Answer: A straight line segment

quiz.q: Why use a compass instead of drawing a circle freehand?
options: Every point is exactly the same distance from the centre
quiz.explain: The compass keeps a fixed opening, giving a true circle.
steps: A circle has every point at the same distance from the centre.
A compass keeps a fixed opening as it turns.
So every point drawn is exactly the same distance from the centre.
Freehand cannot guarantee this → 'Every point is exactly the same distance from the centre'.
Answer: Every point is exactly the same distance from the centre

quiz.q: Which letter can be drawn as one curve without lifting the pencil?
quiz.explain: O is a single closed curve. i, j and = need the pencil lifted.
steps: We need a letter drawn in one stroke without lifting the pencil.
i and j need a separate dot; = needs two strokes.
O is one closed curve.
So the answer is O.
Answer: O
quiz.mistake: Forgets the dots or separate strokes

quiz.q: Which tool makes perfectly straight curves?
quiz.explain: A ruler guides the pencil along a straight path.
steps: A ruler guides the pencil along a straight path.
A compass makes circles and arcs; a sharpener and eraser do not draw.
So the ruler makes straight curves (lines).
Answer: Ruler

quiz.q: A closed curve ends where it starts. Which is a closed curve?
quiz.explain: A circle comes back to its starting point.
steps: A closed curve ends where it starts.
A circle comes back to its starting point.
An arc, a wavy line and a ray do not.
So a circle is a closed curve.
Answer: A circle

quiz.q: When is freehand drawing useful?
options: For quick rough sketches and planning
For drawing a perfect 5 cm circle
quiz.explain: Rough sketches help us plan before an exact drawing.
steps: Freehand drawing is quick but not exact.
It is useful for rough sketches and planning.
Exact measures and a perfect 5 cm circle need tools.
So the answer is quick rough sketches and planning.
Answer: For quick rough sketches and planning

quiz.q: Is the number 8 a curve?
options: Yes, it can be drawn in one stroke
Only if drawn with a ruler
quiz.explain: You can draw 8 without lifting your pencil.
steps: A curve is anything drawn without lifting the pencil.
The number 8 can be drawn in one stroke.
So 8 is a curve.
Answer: Yes, it can be drawn in one stroke
quiz.mistake: Thinks a crossing shape cannot be one curve

quiz.q: A compass opening of 3 cm is used. What is the diameter of the circle drawn?
quiz.explain: The opening is the radius; diameter = 2 × 3 = 6 cm.
steps: The compass opening is the radius: 3 cm.
Diameter = 2 × radius.
So the diameter is 6 cm.
Answer: 6 cm

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'My teacher says a straight line is a curve. Is she joking?'
teach.praise: Chirp! In maths a curve is anything drawn without lifting the pencil, straight ones too!
teach.nudge: What do you NOT do with your pencil when drawing a curve?

revise.summary: In maths, a curve is any shape you can draw without lifting your pencil, so straight lines and circles are curves too. Freehand is quick for sketches, but a ruler and compass give exact lengths and perfect circles.
focus: Decide whether a shape is one curve
Tell closed curves from open ones
Know which tool makes straight curves and which makes round ones
Find the diameter from the compass opening
remember: Curve: any shape drawn without lifting the pencil
A closed curve ends where it starts (a circle)
Ruler: straight curves (line segments); compass: round curves (circles and arcs)
traps: A curve does not have to bend: a straight segment is a curve
A crossing shape like 8 can still be one curve; a letter with a separate dot (i) is not
The compass opening is the radius, not the diameter

learn.hook: With just a pencil, a ruler and a compass, you can draw perfect circles, arcs and amazing designs!
points: A ruler draws straight lines and measures lengths. A compass draws circles and arcs.
To use a compass: open it to the length you need, fix the sharp point at the centre, and turn the pencil all the way round.
Every point on a circle is the same distance from the centre. This distance is the radius, and the diameter is 2 × radius.
An arc is a part of a circle. With a compass you can copy a length: open it to the length, then mark the same length somewhere else.
Two arcs drawn from two different centres cross at a point that is at those exact distances from both centres.

example.q: AB is 6 cm. How do you find a point that is 4 cm from A and also 4 cm from B?
steps: Open the compass to 4 cm.
Put the point on A and draw an arc above AB.
Without changing the opening, put the point on B and draw another arc.
Where the arcs cross, the point is 4 cm from both A and B.
example.answer: The crossing point of the two 4 cm arcs

learn.reallife: Kolam and rangoli artists use string or chalk like a compass, and engineers use compasses on maps to measure distances.

games.title: Draw a circle of radius 3 cm
items: Put the compass point at 0 on the ruler
Open the compass until the pencil tip is at 3 cm
Without changing the opening, press the compass point firmly on the paper where the centre should be
Turn the compass all the way round without changing the opening

games.title: Compass facts
items: A compass is used to draw circles and arcs.
That's its main job!
Every point on a circle is the same distance from the centre.
That distance is the radius.
If the compass opening slips while drawing, you still get a perfect circle.
The radius would change, so the curve would not be a circle.
The diameter is half the radius.
The diameter is twice the radius.
An arc is a part of a circle.
Like a slice of the circle's edge.
A ruler can measure the length of a line segment.
Line up 0 with one end and read the other.

quiz.q: Riya opens her compass to 5 cm and draws a circle. What is its diameter?
quiz.explain: The compass opening is the radius. Diameter = 2 × radius = 2 × 5 = 10 cm.
steps: Radius = 5 cm
Diameter = 2 × 5 = 10 cm
Answer: 10 cm
quiz.mistake: Thinks the opening is the diameter, or halves instead of doubling

quiz.q: A bangle has a diameter of 6 cm. What compass opening draws a circle the same size?
quiz.explain: The compass opening is the radius, which is half the diameter: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.
steps: Radius = diameter ÷ 2
Answer: 3 cm
quiz.mistake: Uses the diameter as the compass opening

quiz.q: Which tool is best for drawing a circle?
quiz.explain: A compass keeps the pencil the same distance from the centre as it turns.
steps: A circle needs every point at the same distance from the centre.
A compass keeps the pencil at that distance as it turns.
A ruler draws lines and a protractor measures angles.
So the best tool is a compass.
Answer: Compass
quiz.mistake: Confuses the compass with the protractor, which measures angles

quiz.q: Arjun draws an arc of radius 4 cm with centre A, and another arc of radius 4 cm with centre B. They meet at P. How far is P from A?
quiz.explain: P lies on the arc with centre A and radius 4 cm, so P is exactly 4 cm from A.
steps: P lies on the arc drawn with centre A and radius 4 cm.
Every point on that arc is 4 cm from A.
So AP = 4 cm.
Answer: 4 cm

quiz.q: Points X and Y are on a circle with centre O and radius 7 cm. What is OX + OY?
quiz.explain: OX and OY are both radii, so each is 7 cm. 7 + 7 = 14 cm.
steps: OX = 7 cm
OY = 7 cm
Answer: 14 cm
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 7 × 7 (49) or counts only one radius

quiz.q: While drawing a circle with a compass, what must NOT change?
options: The opening between the point and the pencil
quiz.explain: If the opening changes, the radius changes and the curve is no longer a circle.
steps: The opening between the point and the pencil is the radius.
If it changes, the distance from the centre changes.
Then the curve is no longer a circle.
So the opening must not change.
Answer: The opening between the point and the pencil
quiz.mistake: Does not link the compass opening to the radius

quiz.q: AB is 6 cm. Meena wants a point exactly 6 cm from both A and B. What compass opening should she use for both arcs?
quiz.explain: She wants the point 6 cm from A and 6 cm from B, so both arcs need a 6 cm opening. Joining the point to A and B makes a triangle with all sides 6 cm.
steps: She wants a point 6 cm from A and 6 cm from B.
An arc from A with opening 6 cm gives points 6 cm from A; same from B.
Where the arcs meet, the point is 6 cm from both.
So use a 6 cm opening for both arcs.
Answer: 6 cm
quiz.mistake: Halves the length (3 cm), thinking of the middle of AB

quiz.q: Kabir opens his compass from P to Q, then puts the point on R and marks S with the same opening. What is true?
quiz.explain: The compass opening did not change, so RS is the same length as PQ.
steps: The opening was set from P to Q, so it equals PQ.
The same opening is used from R to mark S.
So RS equals that opening.
RS = PQ.
Answer: RS = PQ
quiz.mistake: Does not realise a compass can copy a length exactly

teach.ask: Gappu grips a compass with his claws: 'How do I draw a perfect round circle with this?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Fix the point at the centre, keep the opening the same, and turn all the way round. Perfect circle!
teach.nudge: Where do I put the sharp point, and what must stay the same while I turn?

revise.summary: A ruler draws straight lines and measures lengths, and a compass draws circles and arcs. Every point on a circle is the same distance (the radius) from the centre, and a compass can copy a length exactly.
focus: Use a compass: set the opening, fix the point at the centre, turn the pencil round
Change between radius and diameter
Copy a length with a compass
Find a point at given distances from two points using two arcs
remember: Radius: distance from the centre to any point on the circle
Diameter = 2 × radius
Two arcs from two centres cross at a point at those exact distances from both centres
traps: The compass opening is the radius, not the diameter
Don't change the compass opening while drawing
A point 4 cm from A on an arc of radius 4 cm is 4 cm away; don't add the two radii

learn.hook: Waves, eyes, flowers and smiling faces: all drawn with just a compass!
points: Pictures can be built from circles and arcs: a face from a big circle, eyes from small circles, a smile from an arc.
An eye shape can be made with two arcs that bulge in opposite directions and meet at the corners.
A wave can be made of half-circles placed side by side along a line, alternately up and down.
For a half-circle wave on a line of length L made of n equal half-circles: each diameter is L ÷ n, radius is half that, and the centres sit at the middle of each piece.

example.q: A wave of 4 equal half-circles fills a 16 cm line. Find the radius and the centres.
steps: Each diameter = 16 ÷ 4 = 4 cm, so the radius is 2 cm.
Centres are at the middle of each 4 cm piece: 2, 6, 10 and 14 cm from the start.

learn.reallife: Rangoli and kolam artists often draw neat curves and circles around dots.

quiz.q: A wave of 3 equal half-circles fills a line of 18 cm. What is the radius of each?
quiz.explain: Diameter = 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cm, radius = 3 cm.
steps: Answer: 3 cm

quiz.q: For that wave (3 half-circles on 18 cm), where is the centre of the second half-circle, measured from the start?
quiz.explain: Second piece runs from 6 to 12 cm; its middle is 9 cm.
steps: 18 cm ÷ 3 half-circles = 6 cm for each diameter.
The second half-circle runs from 6 cm to 12 cm.
Its centre is in the middle: 6 + 3 = 9 cm.
So the centre is at 9 cm.
Answer: 9 cm
quiz.mistake: Uses the end of the piece

quiz.q: A wave uses half-circles of radius 2 cm. How many fit on a 20 cm line?
quiz.explain: Each diameter is 4 cm; 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
steps: Each half-circle uses one diameter of the line.
Diameter = 2 × 2 = 4 cm.
So 5 half-circles fit.
Answer: 5

quiz.q: Which part of a circle is used to draw a smile?
quiz.explain: A smile is a curved piece of a circle: an arc.
steps: A smile is a curved piece of a circle.
A curved piece of a circle is called an arc.
A radius and diameter are straight; the centre is a point.
So it is an arc.
Answer: An arc

quiz.q: To draw a face with two eyes and a nose using a compass, which should you draw first?
options: The big circle for the face
quiz.explain: Draw the outline first; then the other circles can be placed inside it.
steps: The eyes and nose must be placed inside the face.
So draw the big outline circle for the face first.
Then place the smaller circles inside it.
Answer: The big circle for the face

quiz.q: An eye shape is made by two arcs bulging in opposite directions. Where do the arcs meet?
options: At the two corners of the eye
quiz.explain: The arcs join at the two pointed corners.
steps: The two arcs bulge in opposite directions.
They start and end at the same two points.
Those are the pointed corners of the eye.
So they meet at the two corners.
Answer: At the two corners of the eye
quiz.mistake: Thinks arcs must cross in the middle

quiz.q: Lata draws a wave of 6 half-circles each of radius 1.5 cm. How long is the wave's base line?
quiz.explain: Diameter = 3 cm; 6 × 3 = 18 cm.
steps: Radius = 1.5 cm, so diameter = 2 × 1.5 = 3 cm.
Base line = 6 diameters = 6 × 3.
So the base line is 18 cm.
Answer: 18 cm

quiz.q: In a half-circle wave, the half-circles go alternately…
quiz.explain: Alternating up and down makes it look like a wave.
steps: In a wave, one hump goes up and the next goes down.
So the half-circles alternate up and down.
Both up or both down would not look like a wave.
Answer: up and down
quiz.mistake: Thinks all half-circles face the same way

teach.ask: Gappu wants a wave of 4 half-circles on a 12 cm line. 'What radius should I use?'
teach.praise: Tweet! 12 ÷ 4 = 3 cm diameter, so radius 1.5 cm!

revise.summary: Pictures can be built from circles and arcs, like a face with a smile, an eye made of two arcs, or a wave of half-circles. For a wave of n equal half-circles on a line of length L, each diameter is L ÷ n.
focus: Find the radius and centres of half-circles in a wave
Find how many half-circles fit on a line or the length of a wave
Plan a drawing starting with the big circle
remember: Diameter of each half-circle = L ÷ n; radius = half of that
Centres sit at the middle of each piece
4 half-circles on 16 cm: radius 2 cm, centres at 2, 6, 10, 14 cm
traps: Don't give the diameter when the radius is asked
Divide the line by the diameter, not the radius, to count half-circles
Wave half-circles go alternately up and down

learn.hook: Every rectangle has four perfect corners. Let's build one, step by step, and decorate with circles!
points: A rectangle has opposite sides equal and all four angles 90°. A square has all four sides equal and all angles 90°.
To draw a 6 cm × 4 cm rectangle: draw AB = 6 cm, make 90° angles at A and B, mark 4 cm up from each end, then join the top points.
The diagonals of a rectangle join opposite corners. They are equal in length and cut each other into halves.
Circles with the same centre but different radii are called concentric circles, like ripples in a pond.
Always check: measure the sides and diagonals after drawing to see if your rectangle is accurate.

example.q: Draw a rectangle 5 cm by 3 cm. What should its perimeter be?
steps: Draw PQ = 5 cm.
At P and Q, draw lines at 90°.
Mark S and R 3 cm up those lines.
Join SR; it should measure 5 cm.
Perimeter = 2 × (5 + 3) = 16 cm
example.answer: A rectangle with sides 5, 3, 5, 3 cm and perimeter 16 cm

learn.reallife: Cricket pitches, carrom boards and doors are rectangles; dartboards and archery targets are concentric circles.

games.title: Match the shape word to its meaning
pairs: All points the same distance from the centre

games.title: Always true for every rectangle?
items: All four angles are 90°
Opposite sides are equal
The two diagonals are equal
The diagonals cut each other into halves
All four sides are equal
The diagonals meet at right angles
Its length is double its breadth
It has only one right angle

quiz.q: Kabir draws a rectangle with one side 7 cm and the next side 4 cm. How long is the side opposite the 7 cm side?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so it is 7 cm.
steps: In a rectangle, opposite sides are equal.
The side opposite the 7 cm side is also 7 cm.
4 cm is the next (adjacent) side.
So it is 7 cm.
Answer: 7 cm
quiz.mistake: Thinks the opposite side equals the next side

quiz.q: How big is each corner angle of a rectangle?
quiz.explain: All four angles of a rectangle are right angles, 90° each.
steps: All four corners of a rectangle are right angles.
A right angle = 90°.
So each corner is 90°.
Answer: 90°
quiz.mistake: Confuses a rectangle's corner with a straight angle

quiz.q: One diagonal of a rectangle is 10 cm long. How long is the other diagonal?
quiz.explain: The two diagonals of a rectangle are always equal, so it is 10 cm.
steps: The two diagonals of a rectangle are always equal.
One diagonal = 10 cm.
So the other = 10 cm.
Answer: 10 cm
quiz.mistake: Thinks the second diagonal is half or double the first

quiz.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at O. If AC = 12 cm, how long is AO?
quiz.explain: The diagonals cut each other into halves, so AO = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.
steps: AO = AC ÷ 2
Answer: 6 cm
quiz.mistake: Forgets that O is the middle of AC

quiz.q: Aisha draws circles with the same centre and radii 2 cm, 3 cm and 4 cm. What are these circles called?
quiz.explain: Circles that share a centre are concentric circles.
steps: All three circles share one centre.
Circles with the same centre are concentric circles.
Their radii differ, so they are not equal circles.
Answer: Concentric circles
quiz.mistake: Thinks circles with the same centre must be equal

quiz.q: Which steps draw a square of side 5 cm?
options: Draw two 5 cm lines anywhere and join them
Draw a circle of radius 5 cm
Draw a 5 cm line and a 10 cm line at 90°
Draw a 5 cm line, make 90° angles at both ends, mark 5 cm up each, then join
quiz.explain: A square needs four 5 cm sides and four right angles. The last set of steps gives exactly that.
steps: A square needs four sides of 5 cm and four right angles.
Draw a 5 cm base, make 90° at both ends, mark 5 cm up each, and join.
That gives exactly four 5 cm sides and four 90° corners.
So the last set of steps.
Answer: Draw a 5 cm line, make 90° angles at both ends, mark 5 cm up each, then join
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the corners must be right angles

quiz.q: Harpreet draws a circle of radius 3 cm. She draws a second circle of radius 3 cm whose centre lies on the first circle. How far apart are the two centres?
quiz.explain: The second centre is on the first circle, so it is one radius, 3 cm, from the first centre.
steps: The second centre lies on the first circle.
Every point on the first circle is 3 cm (one radius) from its centre.
So the two centres are 3 cm apart.
Answer: 3 cm

quiz.q: Joseph wants to draw a rectangle with perimeter 20 cm and one side 6 cm. Which pair of side lengths should he use?
quiz.explain: Length + breadth = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm, so the other side is 10 − 6 = 4 cm.
steps: Answer: 6 cm and 4 cm

teach.ask: Gappu wants to draw a rectangle for his nest door: 'How do I make sure it's a real rectangle?'
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! Measure with a ruler, make 90° corners, keep opposite sides equal. A perfect door!
teach.nudge: What must the corners be, and which sides have to be equal?

revise.summary: A rectangle has opposite sides equal and all angles 90°; a square has all sides equal and all angles 90°. A rectangle's diagonals are equal and cut each other into halves, and circles with the same centre are concentric.
focus: Draw a rectangle or square of given sides using 90° angles
Use the diagonal facts: equal and cut each other into halves
Know concentric circles
Find side lengths from the perimeter
remember: Rectangle: opposite sides equal, all four angles 90°
Diagonals of a rectangle are equal and cut each other into halves
Concentric circles: same centre, different radii
traps: The side opposite 7 cm is 7 cm, not the next side's length
Halve the perimeter before subtracting: perimeter 20, side 6 → other side 4
Circles with the same centre need not be equal

topics.title: Naming and spotting squares and rectangles

learn.hook: Turn a square on its corner and it looks like a diamond. Is it still a square?
points: Name a quadrilateral by its corners in order around it: ABCD means A to B to C to D and back to A. ABDC would be a different (crossed) path.
In square ABCD, side AB is next to BC, and AB is opposite CD.
A tilted square or rectangle is still a square or rectangle: tilting doesn't change side lengths or angles.
On dot paper, a tilted square can be drawn by going, for example, 2 right and 1 up, then 1 left and 2 up, and so on. Check that all sides are equal and all angles are right angles.

example.q: On dot paper, from A go 3 right and 1 up to B, then 1 left and 3 up to C, then 3 left and 1 down to D. Is ABCD a square?
steps: Each side uses a '3 and 1' step, so all sides are equal.
Each turn is a quarter turn, so all angles are 90°.
Yes, ABCD is a tilted square.

learn.reallife: Floor tiles laid diagonally and kites flown on their corner are still squares, just turned.

games.title: Tilted shapes
items: A square turned on its corner is still a square.
Sides and angles do not change.
Rectangle ABCD and rectangle ACBD name the same path.
ACBD goes corner to corner across.
In square PQRS, PQ is opposite RS.
They do not share a corner.
A tilted rectangle has angles other than 90°.
Turning keeps the angles.
On dot paper, a tilted square needs equal sides and right angles.
That is how to check it.

quiz.q: Which name correctly goes around the quadrilateral with corners P, Q, R, S in order?
quiz.explain: Corners must be listed in order around the shape: PQRS.
steps: Corners must be named in order going round the shape.
P → Q → R → S is the order around it.
PRQS, PSQR and QSPR jump across the shape.
So PQRS.
Answer: PQRS
quiz.mistake: Lists the corners in random order

quiz.q: In rectangle ABCD, which side is opposite AB?
quiz.explain: AB and CD do not share a corner; they are opposite.
steps: In ABCD the corners go A, B, C, D in order.
AB and CD do not share a corner.
BC and DA share a corner with AB; AC is a diagonal.
So CD is opposite AB.
Answer: CD

quiz.q: A square is turned so it stands on one corner. What are its angles?
quiz.explain: Turning a shape does not change its angles.
steps: Turning a shape does not change its angles.
A square has four 90° angles.
So the turned square still has four 90° angles.
Answer: All 90°
quiz.mistake: Thinks the tilted look changes the angles

quiz.q: In square WXYZ, which pair of sides are next to each other (adjacent)?
quiz.explain: XY and YZ share the corner Y.
steps: Adjacent sides share a corner.
XY and YZ share the corner Y.
WX and YZ, XY and ZW are opposite; WY and XZ are diagonals.
So XY and YZ.
Answer: XY and YZ

quiz.q: On dot paper, a tilted square has one side going 2 right and 1 up. What must the next side do?
quiz.explain: Turning a quarter turn: '2 right, 1 up' becomes '1 left, 2 up'.
steps: In a tilted square the next side is the first side turned a quarter turn.
'2 right, 1 up' turned a quarter turn becomes '1 left, 2 up'.
This keeps the side the same length and at a right angle.
So 1 left and 2 up.
Answer: 1 left and 2 up

quiz.q: Which statement about a tilted rectangle is true?
options: Its opposite sides are still equal
quiz.explain: Tilting keeps all lengths and angles.
steps: Tilting a rectangle only turns it.
Turning keeps all lengths and angles the same.
So its opposite sides are still equal.
It does not become a square or curved.
Answer: Its opposite sides are still equal

quiz.q: On dot paper, Kiran draws a shape with sides of steps '2 right 1 up', '1 left 2 up', '2 left 1 down', '1 right 2 down'. What has she drawn?
quiz.explain: All four sides use the same 2-and-1 step, turned by quarter turns: a tilted square.
steps: All four sides use the same 2-and-1 step.
Each side is a quarter turn of the one before.
Equal sides with right-angle turns make a square.
So she has drawn a tilted square.
Answer: A tilted square
quiz.mistake: Thinks only upright shapes are squares

quiz.q: In quadrilateral ABCD, AC joins…
quiz.explain: A and C are not next to each other, so AC is a diagonal joining opposite corners.
steps: In ABCD, A is next to B and D, not to C.
So A and C are opposite corners.
AC joins them; it is a diagonal.
Answer: two opposite corners

teach.ask: Gappu turns his square cracker on its corner. 'Now it's a diamond, not a square!'
teach.praise: Tweet! Turning doesn't change it: equal sides, right angles. Still a square!
teach.nudge: Did the side lengths or angles change when you turned it?

revise.summary: A quadrilateral is named by its corners in order around it, so ABCD goes A to B to C to D. A tilted square or rectangle is still a square or rectangle, and tilted squares can be drawn on dot paper.
focus: Name quadrilaterals in order; find adjacent and opposite sides
Know that tilting doesn't change side lengths or angles
Draw and check tilted squares on dot paper
remember: ABCD: A to B to C to D and back to A
In square ABCD, AB is next to BC and opposite CD
Tilted square on dot paper: e.g. 2 right 1 up, then 1 left 2 up, ...
traps: Don't list the corners in random order
Tilting does not change the angles: still all 90°
On dot paper, the next side is not the same step repeated

topics.title: Rectangles: reasons and breaking into squares

learn.hook: Four right angles force the opposite sides to be equal. Can you see why?
points: If a four-sided figure has all four angles 90°, its opposite sides must be equal: it is a rectangle.
Reason: the two sides standing on the base are both perpendicular to it, so the top side stays the same distance from the base all along, and the top is as long as the base.
Points P on side AB and Q on the opposite side DC: the distance PQ is shortest when PQ is perpendicular to the sides. Then PQ equals the other side length of the rectangle.
A rectangle made of 2 identical squares in a row is twice as long as it is wide; of 3 squares, three times as long.

example.q: A rectangle is made of 3 identical squares in a row. Its length is 15 cm. Find its width and perimeter.
steps: Each square's side = 15 ÷ 3 = 5 cm.
Width = 5 cm.
Perimeter = 2 × (15 + 5) = 40 cm.

learn.reallife: Doors and windows are made with four right angles, so their opposite edges match and they fit their frames.

items.q: 2 squares of side 6 cm: rectangle length
3 squares of side 4 cm: rectangle length
Rectangle 20 cm long of 4 squares: square side

games.title: Right-angle reasoning
items: A four-sided figure with four right angles has equal opposite sides.
It must be a rectangle.
PQ between opposite sides AB and DC is shortest when it is perpendicular to them.
Then it equals the width.
A rectangle of 2 identical squares is a square.
It is twice as long as wide.
Every rectangle can be cut into identical squares as wide as the rectangle.
Only if the length is a whole multiple of the width.
If PQ is slanted, it is longer than the width.
Slanting makes the path longer.

quiz.q: A rectangle is made of 2 identical squares placed side by side. Its width is 7 cm. What is its length?
quiz.explain: Length = 2 × 7 = 14 cm.
steps: Two identical squares side by side, each of side 7 cm.
Length = 7 + 7 = 2 × 7.
So the length is 14 cm.
Answer: 14 cm

quiz.q: A rectangle 24 cm long is made of 3 identical squares in a row. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Side = 8 cm. Perimeter = 2 × (24 + 8) = 64 cm.
steps: Answer: 64 cm
quiz.mistake: Adds the perimeters of the squares

quiz.q: Rectangle ABCD has AB = 10 cm and BC = 6 cm. P moves on AB and Q moves on DC. What is the shortest possible PQ?
quiz.explain: PQ is shortest when it is perpendicular, and then it equals BC = 6 cm.
steps: P is on AB and Q is on DC, the two 10 cm sides.
The shortest PQ goes straight across, perpendicular to both.
Then PQ equals BC = 6 cm.
So the shortest PQ is 6 cm.
Answer: 6 cm

quiz.q: In that rectangle (10 cm × 6 cm), can PQ ever be shorter than 6 cm?
options: Yes, if P is at a corner
Only if the rectangle is tilted
Yes, if Q is in the middle
quiz.explain: Any slanted PQ is longer than the straight-across distance of 6 cm.
steps: The straight-across distance between AB and DC is 6 cm.
Any slanted PQ is longer than this.
So PQ can never be less than 6 cm.
Answer: No, 6 cm is the shortest
quiz.mistake: Thinks moving to a corner shortens it

quiz.q: A four-sided figure has angles 90°, 90°, 90° and 90°. One side is 9 cm and the next is 5 cm. What is the perimeter?
quiz.explain: Four right angles mean a rectangle: 2 × (9 + 5) = 28 cm.
steps: Four right angles make a rectangle, so opposite sides are equal.
So the perimeter is 28 cm.
Answer: 28 cm

quiz.q: Why must a figure with four right angles have equal opposite sides?
options: The two sides on the base are both perpendicular, so the top stays parallel and matches the base
Because all sides are always equal
quiz.explain: Perpendicular sides at both ends keep the top the same distance from the base.
steps: Both sides standing on the base are perpendicular to it.
So the top stays the same distance from the base all along (parallel).
Then the top matches the base and the two upright sides match each other.
So opposite sides are equal.
Answer: The two sides on the base are both perpendicular, so the top stays parallel and matches the base
quiz.mistake: Thinks four right angles mean four equal sides

quiz.q: A rectangle 18 cm × 6 cm. How many 6 cm squares can it be broken into?
quiz.explain: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 squares.
steps: The rectangle is 6 cm wide, so each square has side 6 cm.
Number of squares along 18 cm = 18 ÷ 6.
So it breaks into 3 squares.
Answer: 3

quiz.q: Can a 10 cm × 4 cm rectangle be broken into identical squares of side 4 cm with nothing left?
options: No, 10 is not a multiple of 4
quiz.explain: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5, so a strip would be left over.
steps: Squares of side 4 cm along the 10 cm side: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5.
2.5 is not a whole number.
So a 2 cm strip would be left over.
Answer: No, 10 is not a multiple of 4
quiz.mistake: Thinks any rectangle can be split into squares

teach.ask: Gappu has a rectangle made of 2 identical square tiles. It is 8 cm long. 'How wide is it?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Each square is 4 cm, so the rectangle is 4 cm wide!
teach.nudge: How long is each square's side?

revise.summary: If a four-sided figure has all four angles 90°, its opposite sides must be equal, so it is a rectangle. The shortest distance between opposite sides is along a perpendicular, and rectangles made of identical squares are 2 or 3 times as long as they are wide.
focus: Explain why four right angles give equal opposite sides
Find the shortest distance between opposite sides
Work with rectangles made of identical squares
remember: Four angles of 90° → opposite sides equal: a rectangle
Shortest PQ between opposite sides: PQ perpendicular to the sides, equal to the other side length
2 squares in a row: length = 2 × width; 3 squares: length = 3 × width
traps: Four right angles don't mean four equal sides
Don't add the squares' perimeters to get the rectangle's perimeter
Not every rectangle splits into identical squares: 10 × 4 does not

learn.hook: Draw a square inside a rectangle, squares that look like they're falling, and a square full of holes!
points: Always make a rough sketch first. Mark the lengths and right angles you know, then plan the order of steps.
Square inside a rectangle: in a 10 cm × 6 cm rectangle, a 6 cm square fits touching three sides, leaving a 4 cm × 6 cm strip.
Falling squares: draw squares of the same size, each one tilted a little more, using a protractor for the tilt angle.
A square with holes: draw the square, then circles at chosen centres; check each circle stays inside by comparing radius and distances to the sides.

example.q: A 6 cm square has a circular hole at its centre. What is the largest radius the hole can have and still fit inside?
steps: The centre is 3 cm from every side.
A circle of radius 3 cm just touches all four sides.
So the largest radius is 3 cm.

learn.reallife: Architects sketch by hand before drawing exact plans, and tailors chalk rough outlines before cutting.

games.title: Plan a construction
items: Make a rough sketch
Write the given lengths and angles on it
Decide the order of steps
Construct with ruler and compass
Check by measuring

items.q: Largest square in a 10 by 6 rectangle: side
Strip left after that square: width
Largest circle in a 6 cm square: radius
Largest circle in an 8 cm square: diameter
Two 5 cm squares side by side: total length

quiz.q: What is the largest square that fits inside a 12 cm × 7 cm rectangle?
quiz.explain: The square's side cannot exceed the shorter side, 7 cm.
steps: The square must fit inside both directions.
Its side cannot be more than the shorter side, 7 cm.
A 7 cm square fits (7 ≤ 12).
So the largest square has side 7 cm.
Answer: 7 cm

quiz.q: After cutting that 7 cm square from the 12 cm × 7 cm rectangle, what is left?
quiz.explain: 12 − 7 = 5, so a 5 cm × 7 cm strip remains.
steps: The rectangle is 12 cm × 7 cm; the square takes 7 cm of the length.
Left over length = 12 − 7 = 5 cm.
The width is still 7 cm.
So a 5 cm × 7 cm rectangle is left.
Answer: A 5 cm × 7 cm rectangle

quiz.q: Why should you draw a rough sketch before constructing?
options: Because it is the final answer
To plan the steps and see where lengths go
quiz.explain: Sketches help plan before the exact drawing.
steps: A rough sketch is drawn before the exact construction.
It helps plan the steps and see where each length goes.
It is not the final answer and does not replace the ruler.
Answer: To plan the steps and see where lengths go
quiz.mistake: Thinks sketches are a waste of time

quiz.q: A circle of radius 2 cm is drawn with its centre 3 cm from the edge of a square. Does the circle stay inside (on that side)?
quiz.explain: The circle reaches 2 cm from its centre, which is 3 cm from the edge, so it stays inside.
steps: The circle reaches 2 cm from its centre in every direction.
The centre is 3 cm from the edge.
2 < 3, so the circle stops 1 cm before the edge.
So yes, it stays inside.
Answer: Yes, because 2 < 3

quiz.q: In a 10 cm square, the largest circle that fits has diameter…
quiz.explain: It touches all four sides, so diameter = 10 cm.
steps: The largest circle in a square touches all four sides.
So its diameter equals the side of the square.
Side = 10 cm.
Diameter = 10 cm.
Answer: 10 cm

quiz.q: For 'falling squares', each square is tilted 15° more than the one before. The first is not tilted. How much is the 4th tilted?
steps: The 4th square has 3 steps of 15°.
So the 4th square is tilted 45°.
Answer: 45°

quiz.q: Shalini sketches a rectangle with a square inside it, touching three sides. The rectangle is 9 cm × 4 cm. What is the square's side?
quiz.explain: It touches the two long sides, so its side equals the width, 4 cm.
steps: The square touches three sides, including both long sides.
So the square's side equals the distance between the long sides.
That is the width: 4 cm.
So the square's side is 4 cm.
Answer: 4 cm

quiz.q: Two 3 cm square holes are cut from a 10 cm × 10 cm square card. What area of card is left?
steps: Card area = 10 × 10 = 100 cm².
Each hole = 3 × 3 = 9 cm²; two holes = 18 cm².
So 82 cm² is left.
Answer: 82 cm²

teach.ask: Gappu wants to draw a square inside his 8 cm × 5 cm rectangular nest box. 'How big can it be?'
teach.praise: Tweet! As big as the shorter side: 5 cm. A sketch helps you see it!
teach.nudge: Which side of the box limits the square?

revise.summary: Always make a rough sketch first, marking known lengths and right angles, then plan the steps. Challenges include fitting squares and circles inside shapes and drawing tilted 'falling squares'.
focus: Use a rough sketch to plan a construction
Find the largest square or circle that fits inside a shape
Check that a circle stays inside by comparing radius and distance to the sides
Find tilt angles and leftover areas
remember: Largest square in a 10 cm × 6 cm rectangle: 6 cm, leaving a 4 cm × 6 cm strip
A circle stays inside if its radius is less than the distance from its centre to each side
Largest circle in a 6 cm square: radius 3 cm
traps: The largest square uses the shorter side, not the longer
Compare the radius (not the diameter) with the distance to the edge
For falling squares, the first is not tilted, so the 4th is tilted 3 × 15° = 45°

topics.title: Diagonals and the angles they make

learn.hook: Draw a diagonal in a rectangle and two corner angles split. Do the pieces always add to 90°?
points: A diagonal splits each corner angle it passes through into two parts that add up to 90°.
In rectangle ABCD with diagonal AC: ∠BAC = ∠ACD and ∠CAD = ∠ACB. The diagonal makes equal pairs of angles.
In a square, a diagonal splits each corner exactly in half: 45° and 45°.
Rectangle from diagonal angles: if the diagonal makes 30° with AB, draw AB, draw a 30° ray at A, a perpendicular at B; where they cross is C. Then complete the rectangle.
Rectangle from a side and a diagonal: draw AB, a perpendicular at B, then an arc from A with radius equal to the diagonal; it cuts the perpendicular at C.

example.q: In rectangle ABCD, diagonal AC makes ∠BAC = 35°. Find ∠CAD and ∠ACD.
steps: ∠BAC + ∠CAD = 90°, so ∠CAD = 55°.
∠ACD = ∠BAC = 35° (equal pair).
Also ∠ACB = ∠CAD = 55°.

learn.reallife: Carpenters check a frame is a true rectangle by measuring both diagonals: if they match, the corners are square.

items.q: Square: each part of the corner

games.title: Rectangle from a side and a diagonal
items: Draw side AB
Draw a perpendicular to AB at B
With centre A and radius equal to the diagonal, cut the perpendicular at C
Measure BC
Mark D above A so that AD = BC, and join CD

quiz.q: In rectangle PQRS, diagonal PR makes ∠QPR = 28°. What is ∠RPS?
quiz.explain: The two parts add to 90°: 90 − 28 = 62°.
steps: Corner P of the rectangle is 90°.
The diagonal splits it into ∠QPR and ∠RPS.
So ∠RPS = 62°.
Answer: 62°
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonal halves the angle

quiz.q: In square ABCD, what angle does diagonal AC make with side AB?
quiz.explain: A square's diagonal splits the 90° corner into 45° and 45°.
steps: Each corner of a square is 90°.
The diagonal of a square splits the corner into two equal parts.
So the angle is 45°.
Answer: 45°

quiz.q: In rectangle ABCD with ∠BAC = 50°, what is ∠ACD?
quiz.explain: ∠ACD = ∠BAC: the diagonal makes equal pairs of angles.
steps: AB and CD are opposite, parallel sides; AC crosses both.
The diagonal makes equal angles with the opposite sides: ∠ACD = ∠BAC.
So ∠ACD = 50°.
Answer: 50°

quiz.q: A diagonal of a rectangle splits a corner angle into two parts. Which pair of parts is impossible?
quiz.explain: The two parts must add to 90°, so 60° and 40° (100°) is impossible.
steps: The two parts make up the 90° corner, so they must add to 90°.
So 60° and 40° is impossible.
Answer: 60° and 40°
quiz.mistake: Does not check that the parts add to 90°

quiz.q: To construct a rectangle where the diagonal makes 30° with AB = 6 cm, what do you draw at B?
quiz.explain: BC must be perpendicular to AB; the 30° ray from A meets it at C.
steps: In a rectangle, BC must be perpendicular to AB.
So draw a 90° line at B.
The 30° ray from A meets this line at C.
So draw a perpendicular at B.
Answer: A perpendicular (90°)

quiz.q: To draw a rectangle with AB = 4 cm and diagonal AC = 5 cm, what compass opening cuts the perpendicular at B?
quiz.explain: The arc is drawn from A with radius equal to the diagonal, 5 cm.
steps: C must be on the perpendicular at B and 5 cm from A (AC is the diagonal).
So draw an arc from A with radius 5 cm.
Where it cuts the perpendicular is C.
So the opening is 5 cm.
Answer: 5 cm

quiz.q: In that rectangle (AB = 4 cm, AC = 5 cm), BC measures 3 cm. What is its perimeter?
steps: Sides: AB = 4 cm, BC = 3 cm.
Perimeter = 2 × (4 + 3).
So the perimeter is 14 cm.
Answer: 14 cm

quiz.q: Is a rectangle's diagonal always the bisector of the corner angle?
options: Only when the rectangle is a square
quiz.explain: Only in a square are the two parts equal (45° each).
steps: A diagonal bisects a corner only if it splits 90° into 45° and 45°.
That happens only when all sides are equal.
A rectangle with equal sides is a square.
So only when the rectangle is a square.
Answer: Only when the rectangle is a square
quiz.mistake: Thinks every diagonal bisects the corner

teach.ask: Gappu draws a diagonal in his rectangle and one part of the corner is 25°. 'What's the other part?'
teach.praise: Chirp! The parts add to 90°, so the other is 65°!
teach.nudge: What do the two parts of the corner add to?

revise.summary: A diagonal splits each corner angle of a rectangle into two parts that add up to 90°, and makes equal pairs of angles. In a square it splits each corner exactly in half, 45° and 45°.
focus: Find angles made by a rectangle's diagonal using the 90° total and equal pairs
Construct a rectangle from a side and a diagonal angle
Construct a rectangle from a side and a diagonal length
remember: Parts of a corner split by a diagonal add up to 90°
In rectangle ABCD: ∠BAC = ∠ACD and ∠CAD = ∠ACB
In a square, a diagonal makes 45° and 45°
traps: A rectangle's diagonal does not halve the corner unless it is a square
Check that the two parts add to 90° (60° and 40° is impossible)
Don't include the diagonal in the perimeter

topics.title: Equal-sided figures: a house and a rhombus

learn.hook: Can you draw a house where every edge is the same length, using only a compass and ruler?
points: To find a point at the same distance from two points A and B, draw arcs of equal radius from A and from B. Where they cross is the point.
House with all sides equal: draw a square of side 5 cm, then from the two top corners draw arcs of radius 5 cm. They meet at the roof tip, making an equilateral triangle on top.
The roof triangle has all sides 5 cm, so each roof angle is 60°.
A rhombus has 4 equal sides but need not have right angles. Draw AB, then from A draw an arc; pick D on it at any angle, then arcs from B and D of the same radius meet at C.

example.q: A 'house' outline (square base + equilateral roof) has every side 6 cm. How many sides does the outline have, and what is its perimeter?
steps: The outline has the square's bottom and two walls (3 sides) plus the two roof edges (2 sides).
That makes 5 sides of 6 cm.
Perimeter = 5 × 6 = 30 cm.

learn.reallife: Ornaments, kite shapes and tiling patterns often use rhombuses: all sides equal, but slanted.

games.title: Rhombus, square or neither?
items: 4 equal sides, all angles 90°
4 equal sides, angles 60° and 120°
4 equal sides, angles 70° and 110°
Opposite sides equal, angles 90°, not all sides equal
3 equal sides and 1 longer
A tilted square

games.title: Equal-distance arcs
items: Arcs of equal radius from A and B meet at a point equally far from both.
Each arc keeps that distance.
The roof of an all-equal-sides house is an equilateral triangle.
All three sides are equal.
Every rhombus is a square.
A rhombus need not have right angles.
Every square is a rhombus.
It has 4 equal sides.
Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°.

quiz.q: A house outline (square + equilateral roof) has all sides 4 cm. What is the perimeter of the outline?
quiz.explain: The outline has 5 sides: 5 × 4 = 20 cm.
steps: The outline has 3 sides of the square (base and two walls) and 2 roof sides.
That is 5 sides of 4 cm.
So the perimeter is 20 cm.
Answer: 20 cm
quiz.mistake: Counts the hidden square top too

quiz.q: In that house, what is the angle at the roof tip?
quiz.explain: The roof is an equilateral triangle, so each angle is 60°.
steps: The roof is an equilateral triangle.
Each angle of an equilateral triangle = 60°.
So the angle at the tip is 60°.
Answer: 60°
quiz.mistake: Thinks the tip is a right angle

quiz.q: Arcs of radius 5 cm are drawn from A and B. They meet at P. What is AP + BP?
quiz.explain: P is 5 cm from each: 5 + 5 = 10 cm.
steps: P lies on both arcs of radius 5 cm.
So AP = 5 cm and BP = 5 cm.
So the sum is 10 cm.
Answer: 10 cm

quiz.q: Which figure has 4 equal sides but is NOT a square?
quiz.explain: A rhombus has equal sides, but its angles need not be 90°.
steps: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles.
A rhombus with angles 60° and 120° has 4 equal sides but no right angles.
A rectangle need not have equal sides; triangles and circles do not have 4 sides.
So the rhombus.
Answer: A rhombus with angles 60° and 120°
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal sides always mean a square

quiz.q: A rhombus has side 7 cm. What is its perimeter?
steps: A rhombus has 4 equal sides.
Perimeter = 4 × 7.
So the perimeter is 28 cm.
Answer: 28 cm

quiz.q: To make rhombus ABCD with AB = 5 cm, after placing D 5 cm from A, how do you find C?
options: Arcs of 5 cm from B and from D meet at C
quiz.explain: C must be 5 cm from both B and D, so use equal arcs.
steps: C must be 5 cm from B and 5 cm from D.
So draw an arc of 5 cm from B and another from D.
They meet at C.
Answer: Arcs of 5 cm from B and from D meet at C
quiz.mistake: Uses a right angle as if it were a square

quiz.q: A rhombus has one angle of 70°. Is it a square?
options: No, a square needs all angles 90°
quiz.explain: With a 70° angle it cannot be a square.
steps: A square needs all four angles to be 90°.
This rhombus has a 70° angle.
So it cannot be a square.
Answer: No, a square needs all angles 90°

quiz.q: Why does the crossing point of two equal arcs from A and B lie at the same distance from both?
options: Because A and B are close
Each arc keeps every point at the radius distance from its centre
quiz.explain: Each point on an arc is the radius away from its centre, so the crossing is the radius from both.
steps: Every point on an arc is one radius away from its centre.
The crossing point lies on both arcs.
So it is the radius away from A and from B.
Answer: Each arc keeps every point at the radius distance from its centre
quiz.mistake: Does not use the definition of a circle

teach.ask: Gappu wants a point exactly 3 cm from both twig-ends A and B. 'How do I find it?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Draw 3 cm arcs from A and from B. Where they cross is the spot!
teach.nudge: What tool helps you mark points 3 cm from A?

revise.summary: Equal arcs drawn from two points cross at a point the same distance from both. This builds a house with all sides equal (a square with an equilateral roof) and a rhombus, which has 4 equal sides but need not have right angles.
focus: Find a point equally far from two points using equal arcs
Construct the equal-sided house and find its perimeter and roof angle
Construct a rhombus and tell it apart from a square
remember: Each arc keeps every point at the radius distance from its centre
Equilateral roof triangle: each angle 60°
Rhombus: 4 equal sides, need not have right angles
traps: Don't count the hidden top of the square in the house outline
Equal sides don't always mean a square: a square needs all angles 90°
A rhombus's perimeter is 4 × side, not side × side
